_sources._all: LOW confidence: built from general regional fishing patterns (tournament calendars, state species profiles, charter-fleet seasonality), not from published monthly catch data; tune with local captains. Season = when the fish are present and biting; legal closures are separate (rules.json). Regions: us-gulf-tx = Texas; us-gulf-north = Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Florida Panhandle; us-gulf-fl = Florida west coast peninsula; us-fl-south = Keys, Miami–Palm Beach; us-fl-east = Stuart–Jacksonville.
_sources.pacific-sailfish: Key used for Atlantic sailfish. SE Florida/Keys winter run (Dec–Mar) is the best-documented anchor (Stuart "Sailfish Capital", Miami/Palm Beach winter tournaments); northern Gulf is summer offshore.
_sources.blue-marlin: Northern Gulf summer bluewater season (Jun–Sep; Gulf Coast billfish tournament calendar: Orange Beach, Venice, Port Aransas in Jun–Aug).
_sources.white-marlin: Summer offshore in the northern Gulf; spring in the Florida Straits. Medium-low.
_sources.swordfish: Year-round deep-drop fishery; Miami–Keys daytime swordfishing is the main US Gulf/Florida fishery.
_sources.yellowfin-tuna: Rig/canyon fishery off Louisiana and Texas year-round, best spring and fall; rare off the Florida west coast shelf (deep water is far offshore).
_sources.blackfin-tuna: Keys humps and Venice rigs; winter–spring peak in the Keys.
_sources.skipjack-tuna: Present offshore year-round; mainly bait for billfish.
_sources.dorado: Florida Straits peak Apr–Jul; northern Gulf summer.
_sources.wahoo: Cooler-month peaks (winter rigs off LA, Keys/SE FL fall–winter).
_sources.king-mackerel: Migratory: spring and fall runs on the Florida west coast; winter in the Keys/SE Florida; summer in the northern Gulf and NE Florida. (Gulf/Atlantic migratory groups, NOAA/Gulf Council.)
_sources.spanish-mackerel: Same migratory pattern as king mackerel, more inshore.
_sources.cero: South Florida reef species; rare north of Palm Beach / Tampa.
_sources.cobia: Spring run Mar–Apr along the Panhandle and NE Florida; winter in the Keys and SE Florida.
_sources.tarpon: Boca Grande/Tampa May–Jun peak; Keys Mar–Jul; Texas/Louisiana summer; NE Florida late-summer mullet run.
_sources.common-snook: Tropical: south Florida core; south Texas (Lower Laguna Madre) secondary; rare in the northern Gulf (null).
_sources.permit: Keys flats and wrecks; spawning aggregations Apr–Jul (when the SPZ harvest season is closed).
_sources.bonefish: South Florida only (FWC bonefish page: Keys and Biscayne Bay, best Mar–Oct).
_sources.red-drum: All coasts year-round; bull reds in the fall spawning run (Aug–Nov).
_sources.red-snapper: Northern and western Gulf core; NE Florida Atlantic. Not a meaningful target in the Keys/SE Florida (null).
_sources.red-grouper: West Florida shelf is the core of the Gulf stock (Gulf Council/SEDAR); scattered elsewhere.
_sources.black-grouper: South Florida and the Keys reef tract.
_sources.goliath-grouper: South and west Florida; Aug–Sep spawning aggregations on east-coast wrecks (FWC goliath page). Mapped for catch-and-release only.
_sources.greater-amberjack: Wrecks, rigs and reefs everywhere, year-round; legal season is short (rules.json).
_sources.great-barracuda: South Florida reef species, best in winter.
_sources.bull-shark: Inshore passes and beaches, warm months; year-round in south Florida.
_sources.shortfin-mako: Present offshore at low density; may not be kept anywhere (rules.json).
_sources.silky-shark: Offshore; may not be kept by recreational anglers (rules.json).
_sources.blue-shark: Rare in the Gulf and off Florida (a cool-water shark); not mapped here (null).
_sources.spotted-seatrout: New species. Bay/estuary fish everywhere; best spring and fall.
_sources.gag-grouper: New species. West Florida shelf/Big Bend core; inshore in winter.
_sources.gray-snapper: New species. Mangroves/bridges inshore, reefs offshore; summer spawning peak.
_sources.yellowtail-snapper: New species. Keys and SE Florida reef fish; rare elsewhere.
